evidence.title: Open EDFA gain spectrum dataset and its applications in data-driven EDFA gain modeling
evidence.publisher: Journal of Optical Communications and Networking / IEEE Xplore record
evidence.scope: 202,752 measured EDFA gain spectra from 16 commercial-grade ROADM booster/pre-amplifier EDFAs across varying gain settings and diverse channel-loading configurations, collected over 2,785 hours; reported transfer-learning gain-prediction errors below 0.18/0.24 dB MAE for booster/pre-amplifier devices using 0.5% target training data.

grade_rationale: This is direct, large-scale empirical evidence that commercial EDFA gain behavior is materially conditioned by gain setting and channel loading, so treating EDFA power/loading dependence as a quantitative variable is technically well grounded. It does not reproduce the protected project architecture, its exact channel plan, launch-power range, topology, or end-to-end readout, and therefore cannot close the project-specific EDFA-P sweep or justify C0. The evidence supports retaining the obligation at C1 rather than upgrading it.

conflict_authority_usefulness.authority: peer-reviewed journal article with an open measurement dataset
conflict_authority_usefulness.conflict: no conflict detected with the current stated C1-EDFA-P obligation
conflict_authority_usefulness.usefulness: high for establishing the need for configuration-specific EDFA loading/power characterization; insufficient for project-specific closure
